newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks seen erring up, peso slightly softer.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks seen erring up, peso slightly softer.

text.p: Traders saw the Mexican bourse opening with upside potential on Wednesday due to follow-through enhanced by a surprisingly large decline in domestic primary interest rates on Tuesday night.
"We closed very firm yesterday and the fall in Cetes rates just has to make brokers feel good," one desk trader said.
Technical analysts situated resistance at 4,540 points on the IPC index, which closed at a record 4,508.79 on Wednesday.

Banco de Mexico placed bellwether 28-day Cetes at 19.95 percent at Tuesday night's primary auction, a fall of 95 basis points since last week. This compares with an average rise of 18 basis points predicted in a Reuters survey.
Traders said they expected the benchmark 48-hour peso to soften due to swaps ahead of the long weekend for U.S. financial markets.
Still, they said falling domestic rates would not hurt the peso, as demand was heavy at the auction and denoted market confidence ahead of Mexico's July 6 mid-term elections.
Dealers forecast a trading range of 7.9350/7.9500 per dollar for the 48-hour peso. Pre-open bids stood at 7.9400/7.9450 per dollar, compared to Tuesday's close of 7.9250/7.9290.

Overnight rates on Cetes were seen easing down from Tuesday's close of 21.75 percent on the market hunch that the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) would not raise U.S. interest rates later in the day.
